strategic_capability_mapping.relationship: Closes the remaining Runtime-owned platform/deadline/durability blocker so headless task execution has durable write, stale-lock, deadline, and MCP crash-window evidence across the supported local Runtime boundary.
Keeps task/run deadline admission, resume-time expiry, terminalization, and durable mutation recovery inside Rust Runtime/store authority rather than CLI, VSIX, prose, or controller state.
Strengthens controlled MCP execution recovery by proving the response-after-receive and terminal-before-record process-loss window with durable Runtime evidence.

answers.strategic_capabilities: Advances headless_autonomous_development, runtime_permission_enforcement, and controlled_workspace_tools by closing the remaining platform/deadline/durability release blocker with Runtime-owned durability, deadline, stale-lock, and MCP crash-window evidence.
answers.new_capability: Runtime can persist a task/run deadline through task.run, reject mismatched resumes, fail closed when an expired persisted deadline is resumed, perform Windows durable atomic replacement and directory sync where supported, reclaim Windows dead-owner process locks, reject symlink/reparse durable targets, and prove the remaining MCP crash window through real process loss.
answers.why_existing_functionality_is_insufficie: RRP-7.1 intentionally left Runtime-wide persisted deadlines, Windows durability/stale-lock behavior, fail-closed unsupported durability primitives, and the MCP response-after-receive crash window open as required-before-release gaps.
answers.product_gap_if_skipped: Brownie could still overstate release durability on Windows/non-Unix boundaries, resume tasks without a persisted wall-clock deadline contract, or lack direct evidence for MCP tool completion surviving a process loss before terminal task recording.
answers.non_duplicative: This is the RRP-7.2 closure for the gaps left open by RRP-7.1; it does not repeat RRP-5.x semantic protocol work, RRP-4.1 durable schema migration, RRP-6 module decomposition, or direct CI workflow hardening.
answers.no_new_rpc: Yes. RRP-7.2 adds no new JSON-RPC method; it adds a typed optional RuntimeDeadline field to existing task.run parameters and TaskRecord evidence.
answers.no_new_summary: Yes. The assessment and audit files are guard evidence, not a new Runtime diagnostic endpoint, report surface, or user-facing summary API.
answers.runtime_behavior_change: task.run now validates and persists RuntimeDeadline evidence, refuses mismatched deadline resumes, terminalizes expired non-terminal resumes as failed before further mutation, uses stronger durable write and stale-lock platform primitives, and keeps MCP tool-completed evidence durable across the remaining crash window.
answers.headless_autonomous_contribution: Headless resume and recovery become safer because deadlines survive process restart, expired resumes fail closed deterministically, and MCP tool completion evidence remains recoverable even if the Runtime process stops before terminal task recording.
answers.milestone_progress: Closes platform-deadline-durability-hardening while keeping Runtime Release Ready false until protocol-event-canonization, runtime-release-guard-ci, and owner license/publish/release decisions are resolved.

implementation_audit_classification.evidence: Durable writes reject symlink and Windows reparse targets, use MoveFileExW write-through replacement on Windows, sync Windows parent directories through FILE_FLAG_BACKUP_SEMANTICS, and fail closed for unsupported non-Unix/non-Windows atomic replace and directory sync.
process_is_alive and reclaim_stale_process_lock have Windows implementations that use OpenProcess and WaitForSingleObject before claiming and removing dead-owner lock files.

TaskRunParams and TaskRecord include RuntimeDeadline; Runtime validates RFC3339 deadlines, persists the selected deadline while entering Running, rejects mismatched resume requests, and fails closed when the persisted deadline is expired on resume.
A test-only child-process abort after durable MCP ToolExecutionCompleted evidence and before terminal task recording proves restart/recovery for the remaining MCP crash window.
The phase does not set runtime_release_ready=true, change license/publish/release metadata, start hosted platform work, or modify .github workflow files.

reject_when: phase claims Runtime Release Ready or changes license/publish/release metadata
Runtime-wide deadlines are process-local only or cannot be reconstructed after restart
expired persisted task/run deadlines can resume and mutate work instead of failing closed
deadline mismatch on resume is accepted
Windows durable replace, directory sync, or stale-lock recovery is only documented and not implemented
unsupported non-Unix/non-Windows durable primitives silently succeed instead of failing closed
symlink or Windows reparse durable targets can be atomically replaced as if they were normal files
MCP response-after-receive and terminal-before-record process loss lacks real child-process evidence

CLI, VSIX, external controller state, prose, model output, raw prompts, provider output, file contents, paths, secrets, environment values, executable content, or process output are treated as Runtime authority

guard:platform-deadline-durability requires Windows atomic replace, Windows directory durability, Windows stale process-lock recovery, RuntimeDeadline protocol evidence, resume-time expiry tests, and MCP response-after-receive process-loss evidence.
TaskRunParams and TaskRecord expose RuntimeDeadline through Rust protocol and VSIX validators without adding a new RPC method.
task.run persists the selected RuntimeDeadline, rejects resume mismatch, and fails closed when an expired persisted deadline is resumed before further mutation.

Windows durability code rejects reparse-point durable targets, uses MoveFileExW write-through replacement, syncs parent directories, and unsupported non-Unix/non-Windows durable primitives fail closed.
A real child-process-loss test covers the MCP ToolExecutionCompleted-before-terminal-task-recording crash window.
runtime-release-readiness audit removes platform-deadline-durability-hardening from release_ready_blocked_by while keeping protocol-event-canonization and runtime-release-guard-ci open.

accepted_capability: Runtime/store own durable write, stale-lock, terminal transition, and deadline enforcement behavior.
RuntimeDeadline is persisted and checked across task.run resume boundaries.
The remaining MCP response-after-receive crash window has real process-loss evidence.
The platform-deadline-durability-hardening blocker can be closed without claiming full Runtime Release Ready.
behavior_evidence: Rust tests cover deadline persistence, expired resume terminalization, deadline mismatch rejection, terminal transition recovery, and durable write failpoints.
guard:platform-deadline-durability and its tests enforce RRP-7.2 evidence through the existing VSIX check path.
safety_boundary: Rust Runtime/protocol/store remain execution, admission, replay, permission, MCP, workspace mutation, durable state, protocol, and completion authority.
CLI and VSIX remain thin transport/projection clients and cannot grant Runtime authority.
Raw prompt, provider output, file content, absolute/canonical path, secret, environment value, executable content, and process output are not persisted as release evidence.
non_goals: Does not claim Runtime Release Ready.
Does not close protocol-event-canonization full strict ledger payload typing.
Does not change license, publish settings, tags, release assets, or public OSS release posture.
Does not add hosted scheduler, daemon, worker fleet, queue, generic shell, arbitrary process execution, remote Git expansion, signing infrastructure, or external platform products.
Does not modify .github workflow files; runtime-release-guard-ci remains a separate blocker.
rejected_alternatives: Rejected docs-only platform closure because durability and deadline behavior need executable Runtime/store evidence.
Rejected process-local-only deadline naming because task/run deadline expiry must survive Runtime restart.
Rejected silently successful unsupported-platform durability shims because release evidence must fail closed where durable primitives are unavailable.
technical_debt: protocol-event-canonization remains required-before-release for strict typed, payload-absent, or legacy-only schema assignments across every payload-bearing LedgerEventKind beyond TaskCompleted known-field evidence.
runtime-release-guard-ci remains open Runtime-owned debt until workflow-scope credentials or owner-approved equivalent CI hardening exists.
Owner license/publish/release decisions remain required before OSS Release Ready.
next_capability_rationale: Return to runtime-release-guard-ci only when workflow-scope credentials or an owner-approved equivalent path is available; otherwise continue bounded protocol-event-canonization ledger payload typing work.

runtime_release_dod: RRP-7.2 closes platform-deadline-durability-hardening while Runtime Release Ready remains false until remaining Runtime blockers and owner license/publish/release decisions are resolved.
runtime_boundary_contracts: No new RPC surface is added; existing task.run and task record semantics gain typed deadline evidence.
CLI and VSIX remain thin clients over Runtime-owned contracts.
external_control_plane_responsibilities: External scheduling, queueing, worker leases, hosted isolation, retry policy, metrics, alerts, SLA, tenant administration, billing, and secret-provider operations remain outside this local Runtime v0 phase.
external_adapter_responsibilities: Forge, pull request, review, notification, SIEM, OTel, language verifier, customer integration, and hosted MCP adapter responsibilities remain outside RRP-7.2.
commercial_solution_readiness: Packaging, distribution, signing, notarization, enterprise administration, operational runbooks, support, and commercial release decisions remain out of scope.
Cargo license and publish settings remain owner-decision items and are not changed by RRP-7.2.
